headline: Nearly 7 lakh fail as SSC pass rate hits 19-year low
summary: Educationists point to systemic failures as girls continue to outperform boys for the 11th consecutive year.
details: The results for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations have been published, revealing a significant decline in performance.
Nearly 7 lakh students failed to pass the exams, marking the lowest pass rate in the 19-year history of the current system.
Educationists have expressed concern, attributing the low pass rate to failures within the education system rather than student capability.
For the 11th consecutive year, girls have outperformed boys in the overall results, highlighting a widening gap in academic achievement.
Experts are calling for a review of the assessment methods and teaching standards to prevent further declines in student performance.

headline: 4,400 bags of cement lost as cargo trawler sinks in Chandpur
summary: A cargo vessel carrying 4,400 bags of 'Shah Cement' sank due to strong whirlpools at the confluence of three rivers.
details: A cargo trawler carrying 4,400 bags of cement sank on Monday afternoon at the confluence of the Meghna, Dakatia, and Padma rivers in Chandpur.
The vessel, operated by 'HM Transport', was traveling from Narayanganj to Chandpur when it lost control and was pulled under by powerful whirlpools near the Big Station Molhead.
Four crew members, including the steersman Ayub Ali, were thrown into the water but were rescued by local boatmen and provided primary treatment at Chandpur Government Hospital.
The owner of the cargo, Hanif Beperi, stated that he had invested all his savings from working abroad to start this cement transport business, only to see his investment sink.
Local residents reported that the confluence of the three rivers in the Big Station area is extremely dangerous and has seen several passenger launches and cargo trawlers sink in the past.
Chandpur Naval Police reached the scene, but Officer-in-Charge Md. Azamgir Hossain stated that the vessel and cargo could not be recovered due to the extreme depth and strong currents.
caption:
4,400 bags of cement gone in an instant. A powerful river whirlpool just swallowed a cargo trawler in Chandpur.

A cargo trawler carrying 4,400 bags of cement sank on Monday afternoon at the confluence of the Meghna, Dakatia, and Padma rivers in Chandpur.

The vessel, operated by 'HM Transport', was traveling from Narayanganj to Chandpur when it lost control and was pulled under by powerful whirlpools near the Big Station Molhead.

Four crew members, including the steersman Ayub Ali, were thrown into the water but were rescued by local boatmen and provided primary treatment at Chandpur Government Hospital.

The owner of the cargo, Hanif Beperi, stated that he had invested all his savings from working abroad to start this cement transport business, only to see his investment sink.

Local residents reported that the confluence of the three rivers in the Big Station area is extremely dangerous and has seen several passenger launches and cargo trawlers sink in the past.

Chandpur Naval Police reached the scene, but Officer-in-Charge Md. Azamgir Hossain stated that the vessel and cargo could not be recovered due to the extreme depth and strong currents.
